text:
Aria Gomez: Hi team, first week here — I opened a tiny change that tweaks a helper and updates README steps for local env. Before I go further: 1) branch target best practice for docs+nonblocking helper tweaks? 2) do we squash or keep history for small fixes? 3) any linters/formatters I should run besides pre-commit?

Ravi Kapoor: Welcome Aria! Target main for those; release/* is only for scheduled hotfix backports.

Marta Li: Squash tiny related commits; keep separate commits if each is its own atomic change (e.g., refactor vs feature). No hard rule, use judgement.

Ravi Kapoor: Pre-commit runs most formatters, but also run `make fmt` and `make lint-fast` to catch style CI rules locally. We have a golang linter and python black + isort behind pre-commit.

Aria Gomez: Got it. Is there an expected commit header format? I saw different examples across repos.

Marta Li: We prefer Conventional-ish style for the repo: scope(optional): short summary. Example: `infra(readme): document local env vars` then a one-paragraph body if needed describing rationale/QA. No need for Signed-off unless vendor code.

Ravi Kapoor: Also: add a short QA checklist in the PR body, e.g.,
- ran make fmt
- ran make test-local
- verified README steps locally

Marta Li: Check CODEOWNERS for reviewers; if none, ping someone from eng or devex. Use labels: `area/docs` + `size/XS`. If you need an expedited review, add `prio/fast-review`.

merge-bot: Merge policy note: require 1 approval from CODEOWNERS + passing CI to merge.

Aria Gomez: Nice, thanks! One more: branch naming convention?

Ravi Kapoor: `<initials>/<type>/<short>` works. Example: `ag/pr/readme-local-env` or `rk/fix/log-typo`.

Marta Li: For multi-file refactors, break into smaller PRs when possible — reviewers appreciate incremental diffs.

Aria Gomez: Perfect, I'll rebase/squash and push up `ag/pr/readme-local-env` with the checklist. Appreciate the quick help! :smile:
